rows.estimation_basis: Estimates are directly derived from reference project id=001-logistics-fleet-portal (3,400 hours total, 20 weeks duration). We reused historical benchmarks for core modules including Auth (160h baseline vs 140-180h planned), Live Map (420h baseline vs 380-450h planned), Deviation/Idle alerts (380h baseline vs 340-420h planned), Driver management (240h baseline vs 220-280h planned), KPI reports (360h baseline vs 320-390h planned), DevOps (220h baseline vs 200-250h planned), and QA/Stabilisation (700h baseline vs 600-720h planned). For the telematics integration, the reference spent 520h across 3 vendors; we adjusted this down to 360-440h for 2 vendors while factoring in the reference lesson learned that vendor APIs require upfront spike discovery and rate-limit buffering.

Because no historical reference projects were provided, this estimate is derived bottom-up based on standard enterprise delivery models. The estimates account for full lifecycle delivery including discovery, dual-vendor integration, automated testing, DevOps deployment, and post-launch stabilisation. Given the uncertainty surrounding the quality, protocol types, and documentation of the two telematics APIs, conservative upper-bound buffers have been incorporated into the ingestion and rules engine modules.

Estimates are directly benchmarked against Reference Project 002-fintech-kyc-onboarding (KYC Onboarding Platform for a Digital Bank, 5,200 hours, 26 weeks). Scope parallels the reference model across document capture, third-party vendor integrations, sanctions/PEP screening, rule-based risk evaluation, and compliance consoles. Estimates incorporate a 15% contingency for compliance-driven scope adjustments and vendor sandbox variations based on historical lessons learned.

No specific reference projects were provided. Estimates have been built bottom-up from standard enterprise fintech delivery benchmarks. Effort accounts for complete software delivery lifecycle, including rigorous security controls, audit immutability, third-party vendor integrations, compliance console UX, automated test coverage, and regulatory stabilization.

Estimates are strictly derived from our historical benchmark reference project 'B2B Marketplace for Industrial Parts' (id=003-ecommerce-b2b-marketplace, 6,100 total hours, 30 weeks). The core domain modules—catalogue ingestion pipelines (620h benchmark), Elasticsearch faceted search (540h benchmark), custom pricing/quotes (780h benchmark), Stripe Connect split payments (700h benchmark), supplier portals (820h benchmark), admin operations (520h benchmark), SSR SEO tuning (340h benchmark), DevOps (380h benchmark), and QA/UAT (920h benchmark)—map directly to the client requirements. Adjustments were applied by removing buyer punch-out integration (cXML/OCI, -480h) which was not requested in this brief, and slightly adjusting QA and core modules to establish pragmatic min/max delivery bands reflecting full lifecycle effort (architecture, development, code reviews, automated testing, DevOps, and UAT).

Because no reference projects were provided, this estimate was developed bottom-up based on general professional engineering experience with multi-vendor B2B platforms, enterprise asynchronous ingestion systems, and fintech integrations. The total allocation includes full lifecycle activities: product discovery, software architecture, backend and frontend development, automated and manual QA, cloud DevOps, security compliance, user acceptance testing (UAT), and post-launch hypercare.

Estimates are directly benchmarked against Reference Project 004-healthcare-patient-app (Patient Appointment and Telehealth App: 3,900 total hours, 22 weeks), which implemented an equivalent Flutter mobile client, doctor web portal, Twilio video consultations, multi-channel messaging, and HIPAA-compliant architecture. Scope adjustments were applied to dental-specific realities: appointment scheduling accounts for operatory/chair constraints alongside provider availability (480-560h vs. 520h historical), while EHR integration effort (420-500h) reflects building an adaptable abstraction layer for typical dental practice management software. Explicit allocations are maintained for HIPAA audit trails, automated DevOps, and clinical UAT/app store release phases.

Estimates are directly grounded in historical data from reference project 'Internal HR Knowledge Assistant (RAG)' (id=005-hr-internal-ai-assistant, 1,500 total hours across 10 weeks). While the architectural stack (Angular, FastAPI, Qdrant, Azure OpenAI, SSO) and core modules match the reference closely, the baseline effort has been scaled up from 1,500 to 1,720-2,170 hours (target 12 weeks) to account for key domain complexities: (1) Ingestion scale and complexity doubled (800 legal memos/precedents vs 400 HR documents) requiring legal footnote/table parsing, increasing ingestion from 240h to 260-320h; (2) Access control in a law firm requires zero-tolerance matter-level authorization and validation, raising security and retrieval effort; (3) Expanded evaluation and QA/UAT to conduct extensive legal accuracy validation and security permission boundary red-teaming.

Uncertainty is addressed by factoring standard ranges for legal document parsing nuances and strict zero-trust permission validation.

Bounds account for standard delivery tolerances while incorporating historical lessons learned regarding query guardrails and builder UX iterations.

Estimates are directly benchmarked against reference project '008-mobile-field-service' (Offline-First Field Service App for Technicians: 3,600 total hours over 21 weeks). That project completed identical functional modules: an offline SQLite/sync engine (760 h historical vs. 720-820 h estimated here), job checklists/forms (520 h vs. 480-560 h), photo/signature capture (300 h vs. 280-340 h), back-office scheduling console (640 h vs. 600-700 h), ERP integration (520 h vs. 480-580 h), background sync/push (200 h vs. 180-240 h), DevOps/release (260 h vs. 240-300 h), and QA/pilot testing (400 h vs. 380-450 h). Estimates are directly derived from historical baseline data in reference project '008-mobile-field-service' (3,600 hours total, 21 weeks). In that project, offline sync and data layer took 760h (budgeted here at 680-780h), job workflows took 520h (budgeted here at 440-520h), photo and signature capture took 300h (budgeted here at 280-340h), and scheduling/dispatch console took 640h (adapted into dispatch web map at 460-540h plus delay alerting at 240-300h). DevOps, store release, and QA/pilot match the reference's historical allocation (~260h and ~400h respectively). Scope adjustments: the ERP integration from the reference project (520h) was replaced with real-time background GPS telemetry, delay intelligence, and WebSocket live tracking (560-680h combined), accounting for the specific operational demands of a courier delivery fleet.
